svg.text: Verilog Gate-Level Delay Modes Comparison
Contrasting Zero, Unit, Specify Path, and Distributed Structural Delay Modes Across Compilation Runs
1. Zero-Delay (+delay_mode_zero)
Forces all specify & structural delays = 0; skips checks
+ Fastest gate simulation runtime (2x–5x faster than SDF).
- Zero timing checks ($setuphold disabled completely!).
- Suffers CTS clock-tree delta-cycle races on P&R netlists.
2. Unit-Delay (+delay_mode_unit)
Assigns 1 precision tick per module IOPATH (e.g. 1ps)
+ Breaks simple 0-delay combinational feedback loops.
- Still risky on unequal CTS buffer depths unless flop CK->Q
uses `#delay` / UDP delay >= max CTS depth!
3. Specify Path Mode (+delay_mode_path)
Uses specify block IOPATH + INTERCONNECT + SDF values
+ Standard IEEE mode for ALL Full-Timing SDF runs!
+ Enables full `$setuphold`, `$recrem`, `$width`, & glitches.
+ Default mode when SDF back-annotation is present.
4. Distributed Mode (+delay_mode_distributed)
Ignores specify block; uses primitive `#delay` statements
- Rare in modern ASIC stdcell libs (which specify `IOPATH`).
- Mainly seen in legacy behavioral memory/PHY models with
inline `assign #1` or gate-level primitive delays.
